title: Call minutes metered from provider records against the plan cap and minute packs, fraud limits (G1 addendum)
goal: Count each agency's call minutes from what the provider actually billed, stop new calls at the plan cap unless the agency upgrades or buys a minute pack, and block the usual telephone fraud patterns.
why: ADR-001 section 7: minutes are counted only when an agent saves an outcome (routes/calls.ts ~411-423) and never checked; R110 added a provisional per-callback count. Owner decision 2026-10-14: calls are included in plans with a monthly cap; beyond it the agency upgrades or buys minute packs priced at provider cost + 20%. No country allow-list, premium-prefix block, rate limits, maximum call length or spend alerts exist.
steps: Master 0024 call_usage (tenant_id, provider_call_id UNIQUE, direction, destination_country, destination_type, billed_seconds, provider_cost REAL, currency, minutes_counted INTEGER, recorded_at). Per-destination provider costs live in comm_unit_costs (channel call_minute, market = destination country, provider, unit_cost, margin_pct) and are entered from the ADR-001 addendum.

services/voip/metering.ts: every 5 minutes per tenant (tenant jobs queue) fetchUsage since the last cursor, insert call_usage idempotently, count ceil(billed_seconds/60) minutes against the call_minute allowance through meterUsage (R110), weighting expensive destinations by unit cost relative to the market base minute (documented rule; weight 1 disables it); remove R110's provisional per-callback count; 80%/100% alerts come from R110.

services/voip/fraud.ts preflight on POST /calls/outbound: minutes remaining > 0 (inbound always rings; inbound minutes over the cap are counted but never block a caller), destination in the agency allow-list (default own country; the platform toggles others), premium/satellite prefixes blocked (static list), per-agent 10 calls/min and 3 concurrent, per-agency daily minute ceiling, max call length 2 h via the provider time limit; never cut a live call.
Spend alerts to the platform owner: daily provider cost for an agency > 3x its 14-day average, or above a platform ceiling -> email and a super admin dashboard flag.
tests: backend/test/voip-metering.test.ts: fixture usage records counted once (replay safe); at the cap outbound is refused with ALLOWANCE_EXHAUSTED and a minute-pack grant re-enables it; inbound over the cap still rings and is counted; premium prefix and non-allowed country blocked; 11th call in a minute blocked; a spike raises an alert.
acceptance: Minutes come from provider records only (code review + tests).
gate: cd backend && npx vitest run   # pass: 0 failed files and passed >= the last merged count (1296 on 2026-10-14)
goLiveVerify: Provider unit costs per destination from the ADR-001 addendum entered in comm_unit_costs; provider-side geo permissions matching the allow-list; provider spend triggers if available.
notes: Before editing read: this batch file, docs/readiness/READINESS-PLAN.md sections 0 and the design note for this area, desktop/audit/fix/FIX-PLAN.md sections 3-4 (executor rules, worktree bootstrap with node_modules junctions; never npm install inside a worktree unless the batch adds a dependency, and then only in the main checkout by the orchestrator).

Backend tests follow the existing pattern (see backend/test/voip-callbacks.test.ts): import env, createExecutionContext, waitOnExecutionContext, applyD1Migrations from cloudflare:test; applyD1Migrations(env.MASTER_DB, env.TEST_MIGRATIONS) in beforeAll; POST /api/v1/test/reset; call worker.fetch(request, env, ctx). isolatedStorage is false and singleWorker true, so use unique ids/emails per test file.

Read docs/decisions/ADR-001-voip.md (sections 4, 6, 7), its addendum when it exists (the owner could not sign up with Plivo; the addendum settles the default provider, likely Twilio where it can serve, with India handled separately), and docs/CALL-AUTOMATION.md (sections 2, 3, 4). Everything here stays behind the VoipProvider interface; do not design around Plivo. Calls are included in plans with a monthly minute cap (owner decision 2026-10-14).
Blocked on G1: the ADR-001 addendum (provider and its usage API) must be signed first.
ownerDecisionNote: G1 decided 2026-10-15: Twilio only (sub-account per agency) outside India; no calling for agencies in India, the Gulf, Thailand, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Bangladesh at launch.
